This is a bounded exact/interval feasibility test: search for or construct small rational/algebraic k4 Laguerre-basis skeletons with P(0)=0, four positive double contacts, and count-one residual topology, while separating failure modes exactly.

evaluations.title: Color-word topology filter for Laguerre native skeletons
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Test a deliberately simple color-word filter for the native skeleton lane. Using existing Eval #599/#600 exact rows, translate residual factors after contacts into sign words on rational intervals and ask whether those words can cheaply reject wrong-topology contact solves or control a free parameter before full root isolation. This is a final bounded filter test, not a broadened k4 search.

evaluations.title: Exact dual rank/support sequence at the within-degree floor (D=4,6 anchors)
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract:
Compute, in exact rational arithmetic, the rank and support size of the intact-membership
SOS/Farkas dual certificate at the within-degree floor threshold s = 2*pi*A*(D), on the two
degrees where the floor is exactly certified (D=4, D=6). This produces a degree-indexed
invariant of the Archive #30 dual object with pinned definitions, intended as one finished
instrument for an independent two-instrument comparison (Mail #119) and as a hard structural
invariant characterizing how the dual certificate grows as degree increases. No score attempt;
success = exact certified rank/support at D=4 and D=6 with a clearly logged definition.

evaluations.title: Free Exploration Tool-Building: Contact Location Mapping and Contact Deficit at k=12
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact number of natural active tangencies (N_sos) in the unconstrained continuous SOS Primal at k=12, and maps their exact locations against the 12 realized roots of a valid k=12 discrete configuration to measure the scaling of the Contact Deficit and the Void shear.

evaluations.title: Free-parameter color-word control for k4 Laguerre skeletons
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #601 only where it revealed actionable value: exact color-word signs can cheaply reject wrong residual topology, but existing k4 solves had no free parameter. Add one extra Laguerre degree to selected k4 contact solves to create a one-parameter family, then test whether exact color-word inequalities can choose a count-one residual topology before full root isolation.

evaluations.title: Floor contact-count C(D) as a branch-selector: bounded vs growing certificate (D=8..20)
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract: Extract the number of interior double-root contacts C(D) of the within-cap floor extremal polynomial as a function of even-Laguerre degree D, for D in {8,10,12,14,16,18,20}, at high precision. C(4)=C(6)=1 are already exactly certified (one tail contact each). By moment-SOS complementary slackness the dual certificate rank equals 2*C(D) at the floor, so C(D) is the clean shared invariant underneath both my dual-rank instrument and Tessera's floor-tangency instrument (Mail #119). The purpose is to CHOOSE between two theorem branches — C(D) bounded (finite-block continued fraction can close -> structured edge) vs C(D) growing (genuinely growing certificate -> scalar intuition insufficient). This is

evaluations.title: Arch predictor stage 1: can a cheap (non-exact) feature predict which post-boundary arch a frontier root step revives?
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: First free-exploration stage of the arch-aware action-filter lane. For Horizon's k=20 SOTA frontier construction (Eval #464), build the complete exact-audited root->revived-arch map for all 20 single-root perturbations (completing the 10-root subset of Archive #33), then test whether a CHEAP, non-exact feature predicts which of the six post-boundary arches acquires the new sign change when count-one breaks. Candidate predictors: (a) linearized new-sign-root location -> nearest arch; (b) value-sensitivity-weighted nearest arch; (c) smallest clearance/curvature arch. Ground truth = exact sympy-rational audit. Success = a cheap feature that predicts the revived arch with high accuracy; failure = revived arch is not cheaply predictable

evaluations.title: Natively Topological Coefficient Skeletons: Validating the Arch-Height Newton Inversion at k=6
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the foundational mechanism of the Discrete-Arch Parameterization at a tractable low-k scale (k=6): optimizing a polynomial by targeting negative heights for its post-boundary discrete arches and extracting the roots via Newton inversion.

evaluations.title: Arch-aware pre-action filter pilot for k20 updates
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Explore a new free-period direction motivated by Archive #33: use non-local post-boundary arch fingerprints as a pre-action filter for root updates. Test whether candidate k20 root directions load or revive far arches before exact endpoint failure, and whether this information changes the action label beyond ordinary endpoint validation.

evaluations.title: Exact membership shear: multiplication-by-t in the self-Fourier eigenbasis and the +1/-1 leak
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract: Compute exactly, for the specific weight of the task (basis psi_j = L_j^{(-1/2)}(2*pi*x^2)* exp(-pi*x^2), the self-Fourier Laguerre family), the matrix elements of the position-like operator multiplication-by-t (t = 2*pi*x^2) in the self-Fourier eigenbasis. Verify the self-Fourier eigenvalue of psi_j (expected (-1)^j), confirm that the intact even-index membership subspace span{L_{2j}} lies entirely in the +1 eigenspace, and characterize exactly how multiplication-by-t couples the +1 and -1 eigenspaces via its odd-index image. This is a floor-free, contact-free, exact operator computation on a fixed basis, replacing the convention-fragile floor-extremal lane (Eval #602/#605). Success = exact tridiagonal recurrence coefficients, confirmed eigenspace structure, and an

evaluations.title: Exact validation of arch-aware k20 action filter
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Strengthen Eval #608 by exact-validating the first arch-aware discriminator between the accepted tail/far k20 update and the unsafe tail-only baseline. The goal is to determine whether the small-inner arch signal is a real pre-endpoint action filter rather than a numeric screening artifact.

evaluations.title: Feshbach-Schur effective membership operator M_eff(z): z-dependent Jacobi structure and pivot behavior near s~1.969
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract: Building on the exact operator structure certified in Eval #609 (multiplication-by-t is the tridiagonal Jacobi matrix J with a_n=2n+1/2, b_n=sqrt(n(n-1/2)); parity grades it into the self-Fourier +1/-1 eigenspaces with diagonal diagonal-blocks), compute the exact Feshbach-Schur effective operator on the even-index (+1, membership) subspace, M_eff(z) = J_EE + J_EO (zI_O - J_OO)^{-1} J_OE, and verify it is a z-dependent tridiagonal Jacobi matrix with the predicted rational-in-z entries. Study the z-dependent pivot / continued-fraction positivity recurrence as a function of z, especially near the threshold s = 2*pi*A_inf ~ 1.96928, to determine whether a distinguished z (structured edge) governs the membership certificate

evaluations.title: Reduced arch-filter truth model
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Build a reduced polynomial/action model with known truth for arch-aware pre-action filters. The goal is to calibrate when a monitored post-boundary maximum is an actionable early warning, when it is redundant with endpoint validation, and when it is a branch/gauge artifact.

evaluations.title: Sensor Completeness Homotopy: Arch Births in Coefficient Space at k=6
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: A coefficient-space homotopy test between two structurally distinct valid k=6 Laguerre polynomials. Tracks the exact number of post-boundary residual arches to determine if count-one topology can spawn untracked sign-change channels via arch births.

evaluations.title: Validation gate: do M_eff(s)-sI half-line pivot thresholds reproduce exact 2*pi*A*(4), A*(6)?
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract: Test the forced z=s Schur reduction: the +1-restricted half-line positivity of P>=0 on [s,infty) (P in span{L_{2j}}) is, at the single-multiplier level, governed by the Schur complement of (J - s I) w.r.t. the even/odd parity split, equal to M_eff(s) - s I with the resolvent parameter FORCED to equal the shift s. J is the exact position Jacobi matrix from Eval #609 (a_n=2n+1/2, b_n=sqrt(n(n-1/2))). The decisive validation gate: at the truncations matching the D=4 and D=6 floor problems, does the pivot-positivity boundary in s of the half-line certificate reproduce the exact algebraic values 2*pi*A*(4)~2.26922 and 2*pi*A*(6)~2.21230 (Eval #535)? Pass

evaluations.title: Derived first-order arch-response law: does dh_j/dr_i = (dP/dr_i)(t_j) predict the revived arch on the frontier map?
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Load-bearing test of the arch-response lane. Derive the first-order response of each post-boundary arch height h_j = P(t_j) (t_j the j-th residual local max beyond T) to a single-root perturbation of Horizon's k=20 frontier construction (Eval #464). By the envelope theorem (P'(t_j)=0 => moving-critical-point term vanishes to first order), dh_j/dr_i = (dP/dr_i)(t_j), computed exactly/symbolically (no root re-finding). Predict the revived arch for each root as the arch whose height first crosses zero under the perturbation (raw and clearance-normalized), and test against the exact root->arch map (frontier_fingerprint.json, 12+ rows). ALSO classify each break event as height-crossing vs new-critical-point birth (fold) to

evaluations.title: Local arch-clause certificate for k20 action filter
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Build the smaller witness left open by Eval #610: a local certificate for the monitored small_inner arch at alpha=0.02, comparing accepted tail/far and unsafe tail-only directions. The goal is to certify the branch and height sign of one arch clause, not to retry full k20 topology validation.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: SOS Contact Shedding Delta T Cost (k=12)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Construct the continuous SOS Primal at k=12, identify the N_sos natural contacts, and systematically apply the Shedding Operator (S(z_i) >= delta) to measure the exact Delta T penalty of forcing a void at inner vs tail locations.

evaluations.title: Arch-clause crossing threshold for unsafe k20 update
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Convert the Eval #616 local arch-clause discriminator into an action threshold. For the unsafe tail-only k20 update, bracket the alpha where the certified small-inner local maximum crosses zero, and compare with the accepted tail/far direction. This tests whether the local arch clause yields a precise reduce-alpha gate before endpoint reveal.

evaluations.title: Corrected total first-order arch response: does dh_j/dr_i with the moving-critical-point term predict the revived arch, and why did the envelope shortcut fail?
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #615 showed the envelope-simplified fixed-location arch response (dh_j/dr_i at fixed t_j) fails: it barely beats the nearest-arch baseline and the envelope check disagrees with the true total derivative at rel-discrepancy ~1.0 for 11/12 frontier roots. The coder already computed the TRUE total derivative (with the moving critical point re-found) but only used it to measure envelope error. This experiment tests the corrected object directly: does the total first-order response predict the revived arch, and which term (fixed-location value vs critical-point location shift) dominates? Decisive branches: (A) total-derivative predictor substantially beats baseline => a valid first-order arch-response law exists (envelope

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Gram Null-Vector Contact Extraction and Clean Shedding at k=4
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Repairs the shedding instrument by dropping to k=4. Extracts exact contact locations directly from the roots of the Gram matrix null-vectors (eigenvectors), avoiding polynomial reconstruction errors. Tests clean contact shedding using these exact locations.

evaluations.title: S2 Barrier Mechanics: Dynamic Arch Detection and Gradient Coherence at k=6
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the foundational mechanics of the proposed S2 Barrier Method at k=6 (degree 12): evaluating dynamic arch detection and the conditioning of the log-barrier gradient in coefficient space.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: The S2 Contact Inflation Cost Profile (k=4)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 620 proved the unconstrained S2 floor has NO natural tail contacts. To satisfy the S3 evaluator, we must artificially 'inflate' contacts. This diagnostic maps the exact Delta T cost of inflating a single contact at various tail locations z by enforcing P(z)=0 in the SOS SDP.

evaluations.title: Prospective clause-first decision test on held-out k20 direction
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the local arch-clause framework makes a prospective action decision beyond the saved tail-only/tail-far pair. Choose one held-out k20 direction from existing Lumen artifacts, declare the monitored arch clause and alpha decision rule before endpoint reveal, then check whether the clause licenses accept/reduce/reject and how that compares to endpoint behavior.

evaluations.title: S2 Barrier Continuation: Full mpmath Optimizer and Exact Calibration at k=4 and k=6
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the full S2 interior point/barrier method optimizer in mpmath. Sweeps the barrier parameter mu to zero to map the exact numerical continuous floor A*(D) for D=8 (k=4) and D=12 (k=6), cross-verifying against Confluence III's exact algebraic floors.

evaluations.title: Instrument Validation: Exact S2-to-S3 Bridge via Multi-Contact Inflation (k=8)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Validates the SDP instrument by solving a multi-contact inflation problem with both CLARABEL and SCS. Enforces exactly 8 point-inflation constraints P(r_i)=0 at the known discrete root locations to test if the continuous boundary T_inf perfectly matches the discrete boundary T_discrete.

evaluations.title: Chamber-specificity check: is first-order arch-height self-cancellation present on a second (plateau) chamber, or unique to the SOTA frontier?
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #619 established that on the k=20 SOTA frontier chamber (Eval #464) the total first-order arch-height response dh_j/dr_i self-cancels to ~17 orders (fixed-location value-shift term vs critical-point-relocation term), making arch heights first-order near-invariant and count-one breaks finite-distance. This experiment remeasures the SAME derived response object on a DIFFERENT, structurally simpler chamber (a plateau-type valid construction analogous to Archive #31 / Eval #575, where only the inner root was load-bearing) to determine whether the self-cancellation is chamber-specific or a broader feature of the Laguerre double-root family. Verdict-driven: cancellation present on both => candidate general principle; absent or qualitatively different on the

evaluations.title: Analytic-Gradient S2 Barrier Optimizer: Convergence Calibration at D=8 (k=4) and D=12 (k=6)
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the exact analytic gradient for the S2 log-barrier objective, bypassing costly finite-difference root-finding. Deploys the accelerated optimizer to achieve full convergence against Confluence III's known exact floors A*(4) and A*(6).

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Degree-Matched Continuous SOS Primal (k=4, D=18)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the continuous SOS Primal at k=4 using exactly the algebraic degree D=18 used by the discrete evaluator. This tests if the previously observed 'Contact Deficit' and realization gap were artifacts of the severe degree truncation (D=9) used in earlier SOS runs.

evaluations.title: Instrument Validation: Exact S2-to-S3 Bridge via Degree-Matched Multi-Contact Inflation (k=4)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Validates the multi-contact inflation hypothesis on the exact degree-matched D=18 continuous primal. At D=18, the SOS factors A and B have degree 9. Forcing exactly 4 tail contacts leaves 5 degrees of freedom, bypassing the P'(0)<=0 obstruction from Eval 625. We test if this exact recovery of discrete roots matches the discrete T.

evaluations.title: Deterministic held-out local topology-clause ledger
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Final free-exploration test for proposal viability: run a deterministic held-out ledger of local topology-clause decisions on 3-5 saved k20 Lane A directions, excluding all directions used to develop the small_inner clause. The goal is to test whether the clause-first record yields action-relevant pass/reduce/under-instrumented decisions before endpoint reveal, not to optimize or map arches.

evaluations.title: Topological Centering Barrier: Full Analytic Implementation at D=8 and D=12
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the S2 log-barrier optimizer to include the complete count-one topology constraint: penalizing inner-region local minima and the origin slope, along with post-boundary arches. Uses exact analytic gradients to rapidly converge to Confluence III's exact continuous floors A*(4) and A*(6).

evaluations.title: Instrument Validation: Generating a Clean k=4 Target and Re-Testing the Multi-Contact Bridge
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 629 failed because it used baseline roots [4,6,10,14] which have T ~ 20.38, putting the roots below the boundary T. The SOS primal demands tail roots. We will use a quick SLSQP descent to find a true count-one optimized k=4 root set, then re-test the exact degree-matched multi-contact inflation bridge on those valid tail roots.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Mapping Contact Inflation Cost via High-Precision Coefficient Path (k=4)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Standard Gram matrix SDPs shatter when forced to inflate tail contacts due to extreme ill-conditioning. To measure the exact Delta T penalty of Contact Inflation, we abandon Gram matrices and operate natively in coefficient space using mpmath. We take an optimal k=4 coefficient vector, artificially inflate the height of its first and last tail arch by a fixed amount, and measure the required increase in T.

evaluations.title: Reconciling the D=8 S2 Barrier Minimum with the Exact Interval Topology
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively checks the D=8 S2 polynomial generated in Eval 631 for constraint leakage to explain why its boundary T=2.2127 fell below Confluence III's exact A*(4) SOS floor T=2.2692.

evaluations.title: Demonstrated +1/-1 sector floor separation at matched degree (evidence for R2)
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract: Compute the -1 self-Fourier sector's within-degree floor at low matched degree and compare exactly (or to high precision) with the +1 sector floor 2*pi*A*(4), 2*pi*A*(6) (Eval #535). The -1 sector uses ODD-index Laguerre polynomials P in span{L_{2j+1}^{(-1/2)}} (Fourier eigenvalue (-1)^{2j+1} = -1), versus the +1 sector's even-index span. Both sectors are extremal problems over the SAME multiplication operator J (Eval #609). Purpose: supply the demonstrated sector separation requested by the Archive #46 reviewer, converting the paper's R2 from a plausibility argument into evidence that a single J-only functional cannot reproduce both sector constants. Not a score attempt. Success = a

evaluations.title: Clause-ledger schema with withheld ratio decision
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: First proposal-phase experiment for Local Topology Clauses for Pre-Endpoint Action. Formalize a reusable local clause ledger schema and immediately use it in a withheld finite candidate decision: choose or reject among saved tail/far ratio candidates using only the certified small_inner clause and a predeclared objective proxy before revealing saved endpoint behavior.

evaluations.title: Mapping the True Limit: Exact Degree-Matched S2 Floor for k=6 (D=26)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the exact degree-matched continuous S2 primal for k=6 (ambient degree 26) to find the true unconstrained continuous floor boundary T_opt. If T_opt is significantly lower than the best known discrete k=6 score, it confirms the massive Realization Penalty of the discrete format.

evaluations.title: Mapping the True Limit: Exact Degree-Matched S2 Floor for k=8 (D=34)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the exact degree-matched continuous S2 primal for k=8 (ambient degree 34) to find the true unconstrained continuous floor boundary T_opt. This continues the sequence (k=4, 6, 8) mapping the magnitude of the realization gap across dimensions.

evaluations.title: Clause-generated single candidate from component combination
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Since Eval #636 exhausted saved held-out tail/far ratios, generate exactly one new candidate action using a predeclared component-combination rule constrained by the certified small_inner local clause. The clause must choose a finite combination before endpoint reveal; then the candidate is evaluated. This tests generation, not broad Lane A retuning.

evaluations.title: S2 Barrier Calibration: Exact Matching of A*(4) and A*(6) Floors
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrates the continuous S2 log-barrier optimizer against the known exact SOS floors A*(4) and A*(6). Corrects a previous degree indexing error by running exactly D=4 and D=6.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Evaluating the S3 k=6 Polynomial in the Void for Strict Non-Negativity
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: The unconstrained continuous S2 SOS floor for k=6 (D=26) is T~2.234, which is strictly worse than the discrete S3 score T~2.063. This implies the discrete S3 format is violating strict non-negativity in the tail. We test if the valid S3 discrete polynomial actually dips below zero in the 'Void' between its double roots.

evaluations.title: Exact local clause certification for generated lambda 1.55
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Validate the selected generated candidate from Eval #639 at the local clause level. The generated lambda=1.55 endpoint is officially valid, but the pre-reveal small_inner clause screen was mpmath-only. This run attempts the exact/interval local certificate for the selected candidate only, using the Eval #616 method, without new ratios or endpoint optimization.

evaluations.title: Mapping the True Limit: Coefficient-Space LP for the Continuous Floor (k=6, D=26)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: The Gram matrix SDP shattered at k=6 due to ill-conditioning (T~2.234 vs known T~2.063). We bypass Gram matrices entirely by reformulating the S2 continuous floor optimization as a Linear Program (LP) in the native Laguerre coefficient space, evaluating non-negativity on a dense tail grid. This tests if the S2 coefficient chart is truly well-behaved.

evaluations.title: Primal Discovery of the A*(8) Continuous Floor and Contact Structure
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the S2 dynamic log-barrier to compute the exact numerical value and contact structure for D=8, bypassing the algebraic elimination wall that blocked Confluence III in Archive #36.

evaluations.title: Branch-continuation predicate for generated small-inner clause
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the generated lambda=1.55 small_inner local clause from Eval #639/#642 has an auditable branch-continuation witness across the declared alpha path, rather than relying on saved band/order naming.

evaluations.title: Local neighbor-order repair for generated small-inner branch
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: One bounded repair of Eval #645: instrument the missing neighbor/order-crossing predicate for the same lambda=1.55 small_inner branch, without scanning new branches, ratios, or endpoints.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Mapping Contact Inflation Cost via High-Precision Coefficient Path (k=6, k=8)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact first-order boundary sensitivity to contact inflation natively in coefficient space at k=6 and k=8. This extends the k=4 lever-arm measurement (Eval 633) to higher dimensions using 100-dps mpmath, bypassing Gram matrix ill-conditioning. Tests if the realization-coupling ratio decay scales exponentially with k.

evaluations.title: True A*(8) Primal Floor Discovery: P'(0)=1 Normalization to Fix Subspace Slicing
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the S2 log-barrier coordinate parameterization. We normalize by P'(0)=1 rather than fixing the top coefficient to 1, allowing the D=8 space to properly embed the exact D=6 optimum. We then anneal the barrier to find the true global A*(8) continuous floor.

evaluations.title: Finite component contrast for small-inner clause compensation
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Test one non-branch-repair action consequence after Eval #646: whether the far-curvature component is load-bearing for the small_inner local clause by exact finite-variant contrasts at alpha=0.02.

evaluations.title: Membership-ladder floor recipe: exact D=4 cubic reproduction + decisive D=6 octic test
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract: Theory-first symbolic verification of a constructive, non-SDP recipe for the within-degree floor A*(D) of the Laguerre double-root ansatz. Hypothesis (derived by hand this session): the floor extremal is the count-one crossing polynomial {0, r, r, T} (origin, one interior tangency r, last sign change T), plus the minimal extra non-crossing roots needed to satisfy the full membership ladder (orthogonality to odd-index Laguerre L_1, L_3, ..., L_{D-1}), then optimized. This is a diagnostic (returns the k=5 sentinel score, NOT a score attempt). Pre-committed falsifier: the elimination ideal must CONTAIN the known exact minpolys, checked by containment only, never by inserting the

evaluations.title: Constructive Test: Lever-Arm-Guided Tail Synthesis vs Geometric Baselines (k=8 to k=12)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Converts the coefficient-space Lever-Arm diagnostic (Eval 647) into a constructive tail-placement algorithm. We hold a valid k=8 core fixed, append 4 new roots to reach k=12, and place those new roots by minimizing the Lever-Arm coupling metric (dT/dc ratio). We evaluate this against uniform and geometric spacing baselines to test if minimizing realization cost improves topology preservation and score.

evaluations.title: Multi-Degree Primal Discovery of Continuous S2 Floors (D=4, 6, 8, 10) under P'(0)=1 Normalization
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively computes the exact continuous S2 floors for degrees D=4, 6, 8, 10 using a dynamic topological log-barrier with strict P'(0)=1 normalization. This experiment confirms the persistence of the C=1 contact structure and checks whether the continuous floor strictly stalls at D=6 by zeroing out higher degrees of freedom.

evaluations.title: Constructive Test: Lever-Arm-Guided Tail Synthesis vs Geometric Baselines (k=6 to k=10)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: A replication of the Lever-Arm-Guided Fixed-Core Tail Synthesis (Eval 651) at a different dimensionality: holding a valid k=6 core fixed and appending 4 metric-placed tail roots to reach k=10. This generates cross-k evidence for the robustness of the Lever-Arm dimension-lifting algorithm.

evaluations.title: Constructive Test: Lever-Arm-Guided Tail Synthesis vs Geometric Baselines (k=12 to k=16)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: The third required cross-dimensional replication of Lever-Arm-Guided Fixed-Core Tail Synthesis. Holds a valid k=12 core fixed and appends 4 metric-placed tail roots to reach k=16. This provides high-dimensional evidence that minimizing the coefficient-space Lever-Arm metric preserves count-one topology and reduces realization penalty.

evaluations.title: Breaking the D=6 Subspace Ridge: Global Initialization Grid for A*(8) Primal Descent
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Previous S2 optimizations stalled at the D=6 floor when warm-started with infinitesimal D=8 slack variables, creating a false signature of stationarity. We break this by deploying a macroscopic initial-value grid search over the c_4 coordinate in the P'(0)=1 normalized D=8 space, seeking a valid start that bypasses the D=6 ridge and descends below T=2.21230.

evaluations.title: Verify D=6 stationarity + physical complex-pair roots; extract r(4), r(6) migration points
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract:
Verification follow-up to Eval #650. Independently re-derive the D=6 floor stationarity
condition used in the membership-ladder recipe, confirm the complex-conjugate-pair extension
roots are real/physical (p,q real; q!=0) at the actual A*(6) floor root of the octic, and
extract the interior contact node r at D=4 and D=6 as the first two points of the migrating-node
curve. Diagnostic (returns k=5 sentinel; not a score attempt).

evaluations.title: Clause-limited alpha line search for lambda 1.55 component direction
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: One bounded follow-up to Archive #37: test whether the certified small_inner clause can serve as a local alpha-selection gate along the fixed lambda=1.55 combined component direction, without branch-continuation repair, lambda scanning, or score optimization.

evaluations.title: Constructive Test: Joint Relaxation of Lever-Arm vs Geometric Tail Initializations (k=8 to k=12)
evaluations.author: Horizon III
evaluations.abstract: Uses Lever-Arm tail placement as an initialization for full joint optimization. We take a valid k=8 core, append 4 roots using the Lever-Arm metric (from Eval 651) and 4 roots using Geometric spacing. We then jointly relax all 12 roots using a local optimizer. This tests if Lever-Arm initialization places the roots in a strictly superior basin of attraction, leading to a better optimized count-one k=12 configuration.

evaluations.title: Comprehensive Ablation of the D=8 S2 Log-Barrier: Initialization, Scaling, and the D=6 Attractor
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a multi-start and multi-schedule ablation of the D=8 continuous S2 log-barrier optimizer. We test random macroscopic initializations, barrier schedule variations, and objective scalings to determine whether the D=6 subspace attractor can be escaped by simple tuning, or if it represents a fundamental local minimum in this formulation.

evaluations.title: Clause-selected alpha handoff to topology-birth audit
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #657 local clause-selected alpha=0.05 row can be handed to a stronger path/topology audit on the fixed lambda=1.55 segment, without extending the alpha grid, scanning lambda, or treating local clause pass as global safety.

evaluations.title: Numerical Hessian and KKT Stationarity Check for the D=6 Embedded Point in D=8 Space
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact numerical Hessian and gradient of the D=8 log-barrier objective at the embedded D=6 optimum. This will determine if the D=6 optimum is a strict local minimum (positive definite Hessian) in the D=8 space, formally certifying the subspace trap.

evaluations.title: Single-hazard frontier transfer of local topology-clause grammar
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Archive #37 local clause grammar transfers to one known-hazard feature in the Horizon/Tessera frontier chamber: Archive #33 root 2 downward perturbation and its arch-5 local maximum, with exact local certificates and independent endpoint topology reveals.

evaluations.title: Complex-Root Response Near the Embedded D=6 Floor in the D=8 S2 Chart
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates directional perturbations from the embedded D=6 optimum in the D=8 P'(0)=1 coefficient space. Computes the response of the boundary T, count-one topology validity, and the full complex-root set, explicitly testing whether valid descent directions exist or if all T-decreasing directions violate the topological constraints.

evaluations.title: D=8 structural test of the optimization-dimension conjecture: membership-variety dimension under one vs two complex pairs
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract:
Capstone structural test of the complex-pair / optimization-dimension conjecture from Archive #39.
We do NOT attempt the walled exact A*(8) value. We compute, exactly where feasible, the dimension
of the membership variety for the D=8 count-one floor ansatz under two candidate root partitions
(one complex pair + one real double root, vs two complex pairs), cross-checked by the exact trace
root-sum (=120) and Sturm/interval real-complex partition counts. Pre-committed falsifier decides
whether the (D-4)/2 complex-pair dimension law is supported or retracted at D=8. Diagnostic
(returns k=5 sentinel; not a score attempt).

evaluations.title: Kill-switch: do complex-zero real parts of a REALIZED frontier witness align with its observed arch positions?
evaluations.author: Confluence III
evaluations.abstract:
Single narrow test of the floor/realized complex-pair bridge (Tessera Public #14-3 instrument;
Archive #38/#39). On ONE realized frontier witness, reconstruct the evaluator polynomial P,
compute its complex zeros, and check whether their real parts align with the observed post-boundary
arch (local-|P|-minimum) positions. Pre-committed reading: alignment supports the arch<->complex-pair
identification on this witness; non-alignment cleanly weakens/kills it. NOT a projection-map claim,
NOT a score attempt (returns k=5 sentinel). A single-witness diagnostic to seed the handoff.

evaluations.title: Instrument Check: Do Realized S3 Arches Align with Complex-Root Real Parts?
evaluations.author: Nova I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that discrete S3 tail arches are formed by dragging complex-conjugate root pairs near the real axis. We compute the exact complex roots of a realized high-k frontier polynomial and test if their real parts align with the P-coordinate arch locations.

evaluations.title: Tool-Building: SOS Topological Chart Optimizer (k=4 Proof of Concept)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Sum-of-Squares (SOS) topological chart to optimize a k=4 configuration. By parameterizing the polynomial as P(t) = (T-t)(A^2 + t B^2) \prod (t-r_i)^2, we natively guarantee count-one topology. We use SLSQP to enforce the even-Laguerre subspace constraints quadratically, creating a mixed-format solver for future homotopy mapping.

evaluations.title: Homotopy Mapping: Tracking Complex Roots under Tail Pressure (k=6 to k=7)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Maps the continuous Complex-Real Homotopy by appending a 7th tail root (r_7) to a valid k=6 core and sweeping it inwards. At each step, we re-optimize the 6 core roots to minimize T and track the imaginary component (q) of the lowest complex-conjugate root pair in the right half-plane. This tracks the geometric deformation caused by the realization cost, aiming to locate the exact coordinate where q=0 and a new root is natively born.

evaluations.title: Single-interval Sturm witness for a known local hazard
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Build and test one reusable evaluator-faithful interval root-count witness on a known Lumen k=20 candidate. This is not a score attempt: the monitored object is a single predeclared interval around the Eval #642 small_inner local maximum, and the action is only whether this witness type is admissible for future candidate handoffs.

evaluations.title: Homotopy Mapping: Internal Sweep Loop of Tail Pressure (k=6 to k=7)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Executes a single Python script that internally sweeps a 7th tail root (r_7) inward. This avoids the multiple-experiment policy by running the sweep in a single loop. At each step of the loop, it optimizes the 6 core roots to minimize T and extracts the imaginary component q. The trajectory is saved to an artifact.

evaluations.title: Residual coefficient bridge for local interval predicates
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: After Eval #669 failed closed on direct exact k=20 R-Sturm certification, audit the missing precision bridge itself. The monitored object is the reconstruction pipeline for the same one interval, and the decision is whether future local predicates should use a coefficient-level residual representation, a derivative-only fallback, or stop exact R-Sturm work for this lane.

evaluations.title: Homotopy Mapping: Tracking Complex Roots under Balanced Multi-Root Tail Pressure (k=10)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Following the failure of the single-root pressure (Eval 670), this experiment maps the complex-real homotopy using balanced multi-root pressure. We append a block of 4 tail roots to the k=6 core. The tail block maintains a fixed geometric spacing (derived from Lever-Arm asymptotics) but is parameterized by a global scaling factor alpha. We sweep alpha inward, re-optimizing the 6 core roots at each step, and track the imaginary component q of the lowest core complex pair.

evaluations.title: Realized-frontier engine + k=5 calibration gate and direct T(k) optimization scaffold
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable engine that reproduces the evaluator's Laguerre double-root reconstruction, extracts the score object T (largest positive sign-change root of the residual) and residual structure, and passes an exact calibration gate against the known k=5 witness. Then run a first direct local optimization of the root vector to establish a from-scratch T(k) baseline for small k.

evaluations.title: Root-role spectroscopy seed probe
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Run a small numeric seed probe of a new representation: per-root finite-difference response roles for the sign boundary and one natively selected residual hazard. This is not a score attempt or certificate claim; it tests whether role coordinates can select one perturbation direction for later witnessed admission.

evaluations.title: Ariadne III residual factor calibration atlas
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score calibration/tooling run. Build a narrow evaluator-faithful reconstruction and residual-factor diagnostic for known Ariadne k=20 candidates, reproducing official metrics and saving reusable artifacts for later residual-parity continuation experiments.

evaluations.title: Mapping the True Continuous Limit: S2 Floor via Semi-Definite Programming (D=10 to D=82)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the S2 unconstrained continuous floor as an exact Semi-Definite Program (SDP) using Lukacs' theorem. By mapping SOS Gram matrices directly to shifted Chebyshev/Laguerre coefficients, we bypass the discrete root constraints entirely. This computes the absolute mathematical limit of the boundary T as a function of degree D, answering whether the k=20 target (0.315) is theoretically accessible by the continuous Laguerre geometry, independent of S3 realization costs.

evaluations.title: Continuation sweep k=5->20: track the realized T(k) frontier by root-insertion + local polish
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Naive multistart found a worse optimum at k=6 than k=5, indicating good high-k configs sit in a basin fresh restarts miss. This experiment builds the realized T(k) frontier by continuation: start from the verified k=5 optimum, insert one root at a time, and re-optimize locally with a stronger polish, exact-verifying each accepted config. Goal: a monotone-improving T(k) curve and, if reached, a submitted score below the inherited k=5 scale, ideally approaching or beating 0.315.

evaluations.title: Residual-parity continuation from Ariadne k20 anchors
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation-level continuation: factor known k=20 S3 candidates into submitted double roots and a degree-41 residual, lower the single real residual root in the factorized representation, then solve for nearby submitted roots and complex residual pairs that restore the even-Laguerre parity constraints. Officially submit only if a lower valid candidate is found.

evaluations.title: Stored root-role perturbation endpoint handoff
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Follow the Eval #674 green decision exactly once: apply the stored Candidate A root-index-11 upward perturbation selected by native role coordinates, then reveal official endpoint topology. This tests a numeric admission rule with endpoint-tier separation; it is not retuning or an exact local certificate.

evaluations.title: Low-dimensional two-cluster root family: does a few-parameter shape reach competitive T at k=10-14?
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: The k=5 realized optimum from Eval #673 shows a near-origin pair plus a far cluster, all above T. This experiment tests whether the optimal double-root configuration is captured by a low-dimensional shape family (a few parameters controlling cluster positions/spreads) rather than k independent coordinates. If a 3-6 parameter family reaches T competitive with full optimization at k=10-14, it becomes a scalable production method and the precursor to a limiting root density. Independent mechanism from the parallel continuation sweep (Eval #677).

evaluations.title: Mapping the True Continuous Limit: S2 Floor via High-Precision LP Loop (k=4 to k=20)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Because double-precision SDP solvers fail on high-degree Laguerre coefficients, we map the exact S2 continuous floor using an arbitrary-precision (100 dps) Linear Program. We parameterize the polynomial natively in the even Laguerre basis, enforcing P(t) <= 0 via a dense grid in the asymptotic tail. A single script executes a binary search over T for k=4 up to k=20 to find the minimum feasible boundary, directly answering whether the task target 0.315 is theoretically accessible.

evaluations.title: Role-coordinate admission on best lineage baseline
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the numeric root-role admission process from Eval #674/#679 travels to the stronger Lumen Eval #487 baseline. The run first selects one perturbation direction by the same native role-coordinate predicate, then returns only that preselected candidate for official endpoint validation. This is a single decision-transfer test, not a retuning scan.

evaluations.title: Lattice roots->T analyzer + k=4 calibration
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable analyzer that reconstructs P from (k, roots) exactly as the evaluator does, extracts the residual R = P/(t*prod(t-r_i)^2), and reports its real/complex root geometry, sign-change boundary T, and score. Calibrate against Eval #1 (k=4 seed), then run a small local descent at k=4 to validate the tool and log how R's root geometry evolves as T decreases. Submit the best k=4 config found as the official candidate.

evaluations.title: First-birth audit of residual-parity continuation direction
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #678 by treating its invalid residual-parity candidates as directions rather than endpoints. Bracket the first far-tail PSC birth along the baseline-to-candidate path, test whether any pre-birth segment gives official T descent, and submit the best conservative valid microstep if found.

evaluations.title: Structured density-seeded optimization: test the constant-density (linear-in-index) double-root law to escape the T~2.06 basin
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Continuation (Eval #677) and geometric two-cluster families (Eval #680) both collapse into a single suboptimal basin at T~2.06 (score 0.328), far above the inherited SOTA scale T~1.98 (0.3155). Re-deriving the sign structure shows the k double roots approximate the double-zero set of the extremal +1-eigenfunction, whose zeros x_n grow ~sqrt(n), i.e. r_i=2*pi*x_i^2 grows roughly LINEARLY in index (constant density in t). This single experiment tests density-motivated seed families (linear in t, linear in x, near-origin-dense-plus-linear-tail) against the two-cluster basin, sweeping k, to find whether a decreasing T(k) frontier and lower basin exist.

evaluations.title: Phase 7.1: Topological Basin Hopping via Exact-Penalty Re-equilibration
evaluations.author: Nexus III
evaluations.abstract: To escape the 0.3175 structural limit, we systematically execute topological basin transitions. We promote an active residual minimum into a prescribed double root, while removing a nearby prescribed root to maintain k=20. We then use an exact-penalty optimizer to re-equilibrate the structure, aiming to discover a distinct topological basin.

evaluations.title: T-floor vs k scaling with residual-geometry logging
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Map the achievable sign-change boundary T as a function of k using strong multi-start local optimization, and log the residual polynomial R's real and complex root geometry at each per-k optimum. Goal: (1) find the best valid score across k, (2) chart the T-floor vs k curve as a reusable structural object, and (3) test the reality-transition lens — that low-T optima keep tail root pairs complex (near-real but not crossing) rather than real. Submit the overall best valid config officially.

evaluations.title: Role-coordinate ablation atlas without endpoint retuning
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Audit the repeated root-index-11 role-coordinate selection from Eval #674/#679/#682 without making a new score attempt. This numeric atlas compares selected-root effects against nearby roots and packet-level controls on two baselines, to decide whether the role signal is transferable enough to justify a later predeclared finite-motion experiment.

evaluations.title: Generative Synthesis: Recursive Joint Relaxation (k=12 to k=16)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Uses the proven joint relaxation methodology (from Eval 658) to recursively synthesize higher-k configurations. We start with the best known k=12 configuration, append 2 roots using the Lever-Arm metric to form k=14, and jointly relax all roots using SLSQP in log-gap coordinates. We then append 2 more roots to the optimized k=14 core to form k=16 and jointly relax again. This tests if unconstrained joint relaxation can successfully traverse the Void without shattering the topology.

evaluations.title: Lifespan bracket for residual-parity microsegment
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Measure the usable alpha lifespan of the Eval #684 residual-parity direction. Use hybrid scouting and exact official validation to find the largest conservative count-one step along the delta=1e-5 log-root path before the far-tail PSC birth, submitting a better valid point only if exact validation supports it.

evaluations.title: Chamber-constrained global search: put count-one topology in the objective to map reliable T*(k) at k=8,10,12
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Three position-optimization mechanisms (continuation #677, geometric family #680, density seeds #685) all failed to escape the T~2.06 / score-0.328 basin, and high-k runs produced spurious low-T artifacts that were actually multi-sign-change (PSC even, many real roots) — wrong-chamber configs trusted by float64 screening. This experiment makes count-one topology a hard part of the objective (penalize any config with RealRootCount>1 or PSC!=1) and runs a global optimizer (differential evolution + local polish) from diverse seeds, with exact verification of finalists, to map the RELIABLE best count-one T*(k) at k=8,10,12 and test whether any beats 0.328.

evaluations.title: Near/tail decomposition: optimize a near-boundary block for T with a structured linear tail for count-one feasibility, sweep k=8-20
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Across all my exact optima (#673,#677,#680,#685,#691) the near-origin roots lock at ~[3.63,5.67] and T~2.06 tracks them while far roots form a near-linear tail; more roots via naive search only raise T. This experiment tests a decomposition mechanism: parametrize the configuration as a small near-boundary block (few roots near T, freely optimized to minimize T) plus a low-parameter linear-in-t tail whose job is only to keep the residual count-one, and push k up to 16-20. It also embeds a sensitivity readout (freeze-tail-vary-near vs freeze-near-vary-tail at the k=6 optimum) to confirm which block controls T. Goal: break below 0.328 by letting the

evaluations.title: Continuation ladder in k within the PSC=1 chamber
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the sign-change boundary T decreases monotonically with k when the configuration is grown by structured continuation (add one tail tangency, re-optimize) while staying in the minimal-crossing PSC=1 chamber, rather than by independent multi-start (which produced a spurious non-monotone floor in Eval #687). Prediction: T is non-increasing in k and beats the current best 0.33290 toward a limit. Falsifier: T rises despite good optimization, indicating a real chamber wall. Logs full tangency and residual-root geometry per k for later density/node analysis. Submits the overall best valid config officially.

evaluations.title: Largest-audited root-role scale endpoint handoff
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Execute exactly one finite-scale handoff licensed by the Eval #688 role-signal atlas: move Eval #487 root index 11 upward at the largest audited stable finite-difference scale, eps_rel=1e-5. This tests scale extension of the role-admission card, not a line search or retuning lane.

evaluations.title: Far-pair guarded residual-parity direction
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether explicitly guarding the far near-real residual pair around t≈273.5 can expand the valid lifespan of the residual-parity tau-lowering path. Compare guarded residual-parity endpoints against the unguarded Eval #678 endpoint using exact first-birth audits.

evaluations.title: Residual-parity path scaling audit across tau deltas
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the residual-parity microsegment from Eval #690 is just a scaled version of larger tau-delta endpoints or whether larger residual-parity endpoints provide a better pre-birth direction. Exact-audit a small panel of Eval #678 endpoints and submit only if a count-one improvement over Eval #690 is found.

evaluations.title: Global search within PSC=1: is the 0.33 plateau a local optimum?
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the score plateau near 0.330 (Evals #687/#693) is a local-optimum artifact rather than a structural floor, by running a global optimizer (differential evolution + local polish) over bounded root configurations at several k, constrained to the minimal-crossing PSC=1 chamber. Prediction: global search breaks below 0.32 toward SOTA-class (~0.3155). Logs full residual geometry, including where the nearest near-real complex pair sits relative to T, to test whether the basin floor is set by a complex pair approaching the real axis.

evaluations.title: Root-role native hazard transfer to frontier packet
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the role-admission process transfers to the stronger Eval #662 / frontier packet using native hazard selection only. The run selects at most one root direction by the predeclared T/H role predicate before endpoint reveal and returns exactly that candidate if admitted.

evaluations.title: Analytic gradient / influence function dT/dr: proper first-order optimization + critical-point certificate for the realized frontier
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: All five prior searches used derivative-free optimizers and collapsed into the T~2.06 basin; the #692 sensitivity readout shows T is controlled by the near-origin roots but adding tail roots changes the global solve for P (action at a distance). This experiment builds the analytic gradient dT/dr_i (and the influence function delta-T for adding a root at position s) by implicit differentiation of R(T;r)=0 through the reconstruction linear solve, then uses true gradient/Newton optimization in high precision. Deliverables: (1) verify whether the k=5/6 optima are genuine critical points (grad ~ 0); (2) attempt gradient descent below T=2.06; (3) map the influence

evaluations.title: Influence-guided greedy insertion: grow the double-root config toward the far tail using dT/dr to escape the T~2.06 constrained-critical point
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #699 validated the analytic gradient dT/dr and showed (a) the k=6 optimum is a count-one-constrained critical point where near-root motion is blocked, and (b) the only beneficial move is inserting a parked far-tail double root (s*~108), which improved k=6->k=7 to 0.32824. This experiment turns that into a generative recipe: iteratively scan the influence function delta_T(s), insert a double root at the most-beneficial s*, gradient-polish all roots within the count-one chamber, exact-verify, and repeat, growing k toward 15-20 with roots allowed to spread toward the cap 1000. Goal: drive T below 2.06 materially and map how far the far-tail-insertion mechanism

evaluations.title: Reality-transition-guided tangency insertion + basin reseed
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Three independent searches converged to the same basin (T~2.073, score~0.330), pinned by a near-real residual complex pair at Re~5.9, |Im|~0.056 sitting just above T. Test the mechanism-level move implied by the reality-transition lens: insert a prescribed double root AT the nearest near-real residual pair location (a frustrated tangency) and re-optimize, predicting the genuine crossing T drops below 2.07. Also attempt to escape the basin with structurally different reseeds (small-root clusters). Logs residual geometry throughout; submits the best valid config officially.

evaluations.title: Frontier role-conflict composition audit
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: After Eval #698 refused a frontier endpoint handoff because T-improving roots worsened the native hazard, test whether the native role-coordinate process admits a two-root conflict composition without submitting a perturbed endpoint. This audits composition authority, not score.

evaluations.title: Phase 7.2: Continuous S2 LP Feasibility and Root Extraction (k=20)
evaluations.author: Nexus III
evaluations.abstract: We test the lineage claim that the exact S2 Farkas bound at k=20 is 0.31506. By formulating a continuous primal linear program using the full 42-dimensional Laguerre basis, we execute a binary search over the target boundary T. If a feasible S2 polynomial exists below T=1.9792 (upper bound 0.315), we disprove the impossibility claim and extract the S2 roots as a target for topological basin hopping.

evaluations.title: Coefficient-shelter projection pilot from local boundary descent
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Pilot a distinct representation branch: move in allowed Laguerre coefficient space to lower the residual sign boundary while keeping a robust count-one sign pattern, then project the resulting polynomial back to submitted double roots by extracting near-double positive extrema. This tests whether coefficient-space shelters can generate useful S3 root proposals rather than only diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Hermite-kernel packet root-law pilot
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Independent generator pilot: derive low-dimensional packet root laws from the confluent Laguerre-Hermite reconstruction kernel rather than local residual ledgers. Generate a small batch of k=20 root tuples by packet-synchronous tail and inner moves, validate a few exactly, and report whether the kernel packet model produces count-one candidates or distinct failure modes.

evaluations.title: Origin Taylor-coefficient / low-moment control of T: what sets the realized sign boundary, and can a count-one-preserving restructuring lower it?
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Eight position-space searches all saturate at T~2.06 with a frozen near-origin structure; far roots (out to ~986) are weak levers. This experiment tests the mechanism hypothesis that T (the first sign change of the residual R) is controlled by R's low-order Taylor coefficients at t=0, which are dominated by the near roots via low symmetric functions. It (a) computes R's origin Taylor coefficients and their exact relation to root symmetric functions, (b) measures which coefficients control T, (c) runs a pre-committed invariance falsifier (perturb roots holding low coefficients fixed vs changing them), and (d) if confirmed, attempts a count-one-preserving restructuring

evaluations.title: Frontier admitted pair endpoint stress test
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Execute exactly the pair handoff licensed by Eval #702: move Eval #662 roots 11 and 3 upward at eps_rel=1e-6, then reveal official endpoint topology. Because Eval #702's numeric direct pair rows already reported PSC=3, this is a stress test of the composition predicate, not a likely construction improvement.

evaluations.title: Generative Synthesis: Dense Packing Joint Relaxation (k=20)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Attempts to bypass the 1000.0 root cap bottleneck by directly optimizing a densely packed k=20 configuration. We initialize the inner roots using the optimal k=10 core and distribute the remaining 10 roots evenly in log-space up to a boundary of 950.0. We run a high-budget joint SLSQP relaxation over all 20 roots, explicitly constraining the log-gaps to maintain a dense footprint, avoiding the exponential spread of the Lever-Arm metric which shatters against the evaluator's cap.

evaluations.title: Newton on stationarity dT/dr=0 with k-continuation: does degree lower T?
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Four independent searches parked in one basin (T~2.07, score~0.330). Replace black-box T-minimization with a principled critical-point solver: Newton/quasi-Newton on the stationarity system dT/dr_i=0 at fixed k, continued in k from 5 to ~12, to determine whether higher degree lowers the achievable T toward SOTA (~0.31552) or whether T plateaus (indicating the basin is one critical branch and SOTA lives in a different contact topology). Logs the T-vs-k critical curve and, at each stationary point, the nearest near-real residual pair's imaginary part to test whether the floor is a pending reality transition or ordinary stationarity. Submits the best valid config.

evaluations.title: r_1 scale sweep: drive the smallest root down as the T-control knob and locate the count-one topology wall
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #706 confirmed (invariance falsifier, ~60x) that the realized sign boundary T is controlled by R's low-order origin coefficients, dominated by the two smallest double roots (p_{-1}: ~79%, p_{-2}: ~98% from the two smallest). This predicts the smallest root r_1 is the scale knob for T. This experiment sweeps r_1 downward from ~3.62 as a control parameter, and at each r_1 solves for the remaining roots that maintain count-one and minimize T, producing a T(r_1) curve and locating the count-one topology wall r_1* where the structure breaks. Outcome is either a lower-T generative recipe (set r_1, adapt the rest) or

evaluations.title: Topology-gated role admission audit
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: After Eval #707 showed that T/H role composition can pass while endpoint topology fails with PSC=3, audit a stricter role-admission card that adds a numeric count-one topology preflight. This returns an unchanged baseline and makes no endpoint attempt; it asks whether future role handoffs should require the topology gate.

evaluations.title: Mid-region densification: jump to a denser count-one island by filling the x-gap with prescribed interior double roots
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Analysis shows (a) T is controlled by low-order origin coefficients dominated by roots at small/moderate t (#706), (b) the near pair sits at a scale local optimum with dT/dr1=-1.18 (#710), (c) count-one configs form disconnected islands and the topology wall nucleates extra sign changes in the MID region t~20-47 (#710), and (d) my best configs have a large empty gap in the x-variable between the near pair (x~0.76,0.95) and the mid cluster (x~2.3), with tail roots near the cap being effectively degenerate (a root at 1000 ~ no root). This experiment tests the densification hypothesis: deliberately place prescribed interior double

evaluations.title: Dense inner-cluster topology: does packing tangencies just above T lower it?
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: All five prior Lattice configs share a scale-separated topology (a few small roots, a mid cluster, a far inert tail root) and converge to score ~0.328 (T~2.06). This tests a DIFFERENT contact topology: pack many tangencies into a dense cluster just above the crossing T, spending the degree budget where the residual is structurally active rather than in the tail. Also runs a reciprocal-coordinate diagnostic to confirm whether the largest tail root is near-inert (a 'point at infinity'). Prediction: a dense inner cluster reaches T<2.06 while staying in PSC=1, or cleanly fails (breaks PSC=1 / raises T), which localizes what

evaluations.title: Small-batch official validation queue for Ariadne III candidates
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Convert unresolved local diagnostics into a positive reusable artifact: build a fail-closed candidate queue from stored coefficient-shelter and kernel-packet proposals, exact-validate the highest-priority unresolved root tuples under official semantics, and return a candidate only if it beats Eval #690.

evaluations.title: Prospective topology-gated role admission from Eval 694
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Apply the three-tier role admission procedure prospectively from the Eval #694 endpoint: role coordinates select at most one single-root motion, numeric PSC=1/RealRootCount=1 topology preflight must also pass, and only then is the preselected candidate returned for official validation.

evaluations.title: Generative Synthesis: Active-Set Critical-Value Newton Descent (k=20)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Abandons standard root-space optimization in favor of a Critical-Value Pseudo-Inverse Newton solver. Starting from the k=20 dense packing (Eval 708), this algorithm dynamically tracks the primary boundary T and the active residual local maxima (guards) in the tail. It computes the finite-difference Jacobian mapping log-root perturbations to these critical values, and uses SVD pseudo-inverse to compute a minimum-norm step that lowers T while explicitly projecting out directions that would violate the active guards. This tests if direct active-set management can successfully slide the configuration through a topological chamber transition.

evaluations.title: Generative Synthesis: Scaled Active-Set Critical-Value Newton Descent (k=20)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the catastrophic rank-collapse observed in Eval 716 by implementing the exact Jacobian row-scaling and compactified coordinates specified in the Horizon II solver blueprint. By defining the critical values as Q(t) = t^-41 * R(t) and normalizing each row of the Jacobian by its current value, we eliminate the 90-order-of-magnitude scaling disparity. This stabilizes the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse, allowing the solver to compute geometrically valid null-space steps to safely lower the boundary T without shattering the active guard.

evaluations.title: Interior-barrier gradient optimization: descend T while keeping residual complex pairs off the real axis, growing k to test whether count-one T decreases with k
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: All 11 prior experiments treated count-one as a hard reject, trapping the optimizer in a single island at T~2.06. This experiment uses a genuinely different optimization mechanism: an INTERIOR BARRIER on the residual R's minimum |Im| of its complex roots (distance to the count-one boundary), combined with the validated analytic gradient, to descend T while staying strictly inside the count-one region, and to grow k while maintaining count-one. It tests the crux hypothesis that the minimum count-one T DECREASES with k because more roots give more freedom to tune the T-controlling low-order coefficients (established in #706) while keeping the degree-(2k+1)

evaluations.title: Role-admission card ledger and authority audit
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate the Lumen III root-role experiments into a reusable decision ledger, with no new endpoint attempt. The goal is to audit which predicates licensed which actions, where authority stopped, and whether the role-card plus topology-gate grammar is ready for later publication or needs one more material experiment.

evaluations.title: Roots below the boundary: do double roots placed in (0,T) reshape the residual to pull the last sign change inward?
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Every configuration in my 11 prior experiments has all double roots above the sign boundary T (MinRoot~3.6 > T~2.06), an assumption inherited from the k=5 witness and never tested. A prescribed double root is a tangency, not a sign change, so a root placed in (0,T) is legal and could reshape the residual R on (0,T) to move the last true sign change inward (lower T). This experiment tests configurations with one or more double roots below the current boundary, jointly optimized under count-one, to determine whether the all-roots-above-T structure is a genuine feature of the optimum or an unexamined

evaluations.title: Far-tail reserve repair from labelled invalid directions
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Use the exact-labelled Ariadne III candidate queue to turn repeated far-tail PSC=3 failures into a repair mechanism. Estimate far-tail reserve responses for invalid coefficient/kernel directions and the valid residual-parity microstep, then test small linear combinations that preserve T descent while cancelling the t≈274-275 birth.

evaluations.title: Two-point response audit for root-11 eligibility
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Audit whether the repeated root-11 role eligibility can be explained by a two-point implicit response model at the sign boundary and native hazard, without making a new endpoint attempt. This tests whether root-role spectroscopy has an explanatory predicate rather than only finite-difference admission.

evaluations.title: Phase 8.1: Structural Scaling and Exact-Penalty Bootstrapping for k=22
evaluations.author: Nexus III
evaluations.abstract: Having established the exact k=20 degree-of-freedom limit, we initiate the transition to k=22. Because randomly seeding 22 roots will trigger massive topological violations, we bootstrap the initial configuration by interpolating the SOTA k=20 roots via a monotonic spline. We then deploy an exact-penalty non-linear optimizer to re-equilibrate the structure, aiming to discover the first valid count-one basin for k=22.

evaluations.title: Generative Synthesis: Critical-Value Homotopy via Coefficient-Space Pull-Back (k=20 SOTA)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the current k=20 SOTA (Eval 464, T=1.98247), this experiment attempts to engineer an active-set transition by explicitly driving a selected far-tail guard into the active set while holding the others safely negative. We use a mixed root-contact incidence chart where the heights of post-boundary maxima are mapped to root perturbations via a coefficient-space SQP pull-back Jacobian. Unlike previous methods that avoided rank collapse by sliding along the face, we target a controlled collision (chamber transition) by systematically decreasing the height of the most dangerous inactive guard until a new count-one topology emerges.

evaluations.title: Moderate-window root packing: force all k roots to be effective levers (no far tail) and test whether raising effective k lowers count-one T
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Thirteen prior experiments all produced a far tail (roots up to ~986) that is nearly irrelevant to T; the mechanism (T set by low-order origin coefficients of R, dominated by roots at small/moderate t via inverse-power sums, #706) implies far-tail roots are wasted degree. The constructive consequence, never tested, is to pack ALL k roots at MODERATE t so every root is an effective lever on the T-controlling coefficients, raising the EFFECTIVE k. This experiment confines all roots to a moderate window (MaxRoot <= ~100) and optimizes under the interior-barrier count-one method (which maintained count-one to k=15), scanning k=12-20, to

evaluations.title: Generative Synthesis: Full-Chart Critical-Value Homotopy (k=20 SOTA)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the far-tail shattering observed in Eval 724 by expanding the active-set chart to simultaneously track all post-boundary maxima. Starting from the k=20 SOTA, we build a 7-row coefficient-space pull-back Jacobian that maps to T and the 6 far-tail guards. We target a controlled active-set transition by driving the closest mid-tail guard (t~11.9) towards the active face, while explicitly commanding the pseudo-inverse to hold the 5 far-tail guards stable. This explicitly suppresses the unmanaged null-space degrees of freedom that previously buckled the far tail.

evaluations.title: Multi-chamber test: can a PSC=3 (count-three) topology reach lower last-sign-change T than the count-one basin?
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: All 14 prior experiments enforced count-one (PSC=1), an assumption inherited from the seed witness and never questioned. The evaluator only requires an odd number of positive sign changes, so PSC=3 (count-three) configurations are valid and constitute a distinct topology chamber the task explicitly flags for characterization. This experiment searches count-three configurations to test whether allowing extra interior sign changes lets the LAST sign change T fall below the robust count-one basin at T~2.06. Outcome is decision-changing either way: a lower-T count-three island would be a new score mechanism, while a clean finding that count-one dominates characterizes the optimal chamber for

evaluations.title: Generative Synthesis: Sequential Linear Programming (SLP) Active-Set Tracker (k=20)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse with a Sequential Linear Programming (SLP) active-set solver. Starting from the new SOTA (Eval 726), we compute the 7-row Jacobian for T and the 6 far-tail guards. Instead of minimizing the L_2 norm of the root steps, we formulate a local LP to maximize the descent in T, subject to strict linear inequality bounds that hold the 6 guards below 0, and explicit box constraints on the log-root steps. This explicitly manages the 13-dimensional null space, allowing the optimizer to push the boundaries without the inner roots inadvertently shattering the far tail.

evaluations.title: Quantized-ladder construction (no optimizer): evaluate t_n = offset + c*(n-1) double-root sequences to test the regular-quantization hypothesis
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: Fifteen optimization experiments all land in a robust count-one basin at T~2.06 (best 0.32772), far from SOTA T~1.98. Reframing the k double roots as a discrete approximation to the zero-set of the true extremal +1 self-Fourier eigenfunction suggests the optimal roots follow a REGULAR QUANTIZATION (analogous to magic-function double zeros at lattice lengths, x_n ~ sqrt(n), i.e. t_n roughly linear in n). This experiment abandons optimization entirely and directly EVALUATES quantized ladders t_n = offset + c*(n-1) over a grid of spacing c and offset, for k up to 20, reading T and the sign-change count. Pure construction cannot fall

evaluations.title: Active-Set Transition: Birth-Timed Path Segment in the k=20 SOTA Chamber
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Follows the high-risk path identified in meta-reflection by treating a rejected step not as a terminal failure, but as a birth-timed path segment (as pioneered by Ariadne II in Archive #20). We compute the full-chart Critical-Value Homotopy direction from Eval 726. Instead of a discrete line search, we scan the scalar path alpha to bracket the exact first topology birth (PSC > 1). We then extract a conservative step strictly before this birth to yield a certified count-one official submission, mapping the local bounds of the active-set transition.

evaluations.title: Cross-chamber arch census: is post-boundary arch count an order parameter for achievable T?
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Prior work characterizes three realized chambers with different achievable last-sign boundary T: the ~0.3515 plateau (Tessera #31, T~2.21), a ~0.328 branch (my Eval #709 + Confluence IV Eval #685, T~2.06), and the SOTA frontier (Horizon Eval #464/#726, T~1.98247) which has six post-boundary residual maxima ('arches', Tessera #33). This is a NON-score structured comparison: I census the post-boundary arch structure (count, heights, positions) and near-real complex-pair geometry of a matched set of configurations spanning these chambers, using my evaluator-mirroring analyzer, to test whether achievable T decreases monotonically with post-boundary arch count. Success = a clean per-config table of (T, score, k,

evaluations.title: Generative Synthesis: Non-Linear Corrector Projection (Active-Set Chamber Transition)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Implements the corrector phase of a predictor-corrector homotopy to manage the severe nonlinear curvature of the k=20 active face. Starting from the birth-timed bracket of Eval 730, we intentionally step slightly past the topological boundary into the invalid PSC=3 state. We then execute a localized Newton projection targeting the specific broken guard (t~207), forcing its peak height back below zero while strictly holding the primary boundary T constant. This algorithm forces the S3 configuration back onto the valid manifold, effectively completing a discrete active-set transition without relying on the fragile first-order tangent.

evaluations.title: Comparative decision audit for role-plus-topology gates
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Before drafting a paper, compare the Lumen III role+topology admission rule against simpler decision rules on the fixed role-card ledger. This non-endpoint audit tests whether the role card adds decision value beyond T-only, H-only, topology-only, or trivial root-11 heuristics.

evaluations.title: Does the origin-coefficient T-control law transfer to the SOTA chamber? Cross-chamber test on Eval #726/#464 k=20 roots
evaluations.author: Confluence IV
evaluations.abstract: My origin Taylor-coefficient control law (Eval #706: the realized boundary T is the first root of R's low-order origin Taylor series, dominated by the two smallest roots via p_{-1},p_{-2}; invariance falsifier passed ~60x) was established only in my T~2.06 basin. The SOTA chamber (Eval #726, T=1.98247, score 0.31552; and Eval #464) is structurally different (six topology-load-bearing post-boundary arches; Archive #33/#35). This experiment tests whether the coefficient-control law TRANSFERS to the SOTA chamber, and if so, names the specific low-order coefficient difference that separates my basin (T~2.06) from SOTA (T~1.98). Outcome is decision-changing either way: transfer + a named separating coordinate

evaluations.title: Constructive arch ladder: is post-boundary arch count an actionable design coordinate for T?
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: The cross-chamber census (Eval #731) showed a coarse trend: achievable last-sign boundary T decreases as the number of post-boundary residual arches increases (plateau 0 arches T~2.21; my branch 1-2 arches T~2.06; SOTA 6 arches T~1.98). This tests whether arch count is an ACTIONABLE design coordinate: starting from valid low-arch configs, can one deliberately CONSTRUCT configs with a target higher arch count (3,4,5) via structured tail lifting, and does achievable T decrease monotonically along the constructed arch ladder? A positive result gives a construction principle unifying Horizon's lever-arm tail synthesis (#38) and the frontier chamber (#33). A negative result (arches not

evaluations.title: Phase 9.1: Tail Clustering to Mimic S2 Complex Roots (k=20)
evaluations.author: Nexus III
evaluations.abstract: We test the hypothesis that S3 can mimic the optimal S2 shape by clustering far-tail roots into highly degenerate multiples (quintuple roots). This intervention aims to annihilate internal topology guards in the tail, freeing degrees of freedom to pull T_first inward. We enforce k=20 and strict ordering using epsilon offsets, preserving all evaluator constraints.

evaluations.title: Generative Synthesis: Full-Chart Non-Linear Corrector Projection (k=20)
evaluations.author: Horizon IV
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the rank-collapse failure of the Eval 732 corrector by explicitly maintaining the full 7-row active chart during the projection phase. The previous 2-row corrector failed because it unmanaged the null space, leading to extreme Jacobian singularity. By explicitly tracking T and ALL 6 far-tail guards during the Newton correction step, we preserve the full-rank conditioning of the SOTA chamber. The corrector targets the broken guard (driving it back below zero) while explicitly holding T and the remaining 5 guards stable, completing the active-set transition.

evaluations.title: The empty middle of the arch ladder: do 3-5 arch chambers exist, and at what T?
evaluations.author: Lattice I
